Steph — thanks for looping us in. Short answer: 45ms p95 across multi-region for gen calls is very aggressive for general-purpose hosted tiers. That said, it's technically achievable if Orion is willing to:

- Move to a Dedicated reserved pool with regional placement in us-west and us-east (no shared tenancy).
- Accept a configuration with hot warm-pools (pre-warmed serving instances) + aggressive KV prefix caching for repeated prompt patterns.
- Commit to a minimal sustained throughput (requests/sec) to justify warm capacity — otherwise cold-starts will blow p95.

Trade-offs / risks:
- Cost: dedicated pool + warm pools increases unit cost — roughly +30–50% on inference spend relative to hosted API for same token volume; plus an additional monthly reserved fee for capacity guarantees.
- Operational: requires enhanced SRE runbook and a 24/7 escalation pager during launch window; we should include an optional on-premises routing fallback for cross-region failover.
- Guarantees: even with Dedicated, we can promise 99.95% uptime and p95 <= 60ms for generation traffic in the US, provided the dedicated pool is correctly sized. Hitting 99.995% and 45ms p95 would require extreme overprovisioning and a higher uplift — I estimate ~+80–120% cost and some architectural changes to kernel scheduling and routing policies.

Action items I recommend:
1) Offer a phased SLA: 99.95% + p95 <= 60ms for 90 days (pilot), then revisit to tighten to 99.99% / 50ms if observational metrics support it.
2) If Orion insists on 99.995%/45ms, require a dedicated warm pool with 3-region active/passive failover and a ~1.8x capacity commit.
3) Draft clear performance measurement definitions (which endpoints, tokenization rules, client-side retries).

I'll ping infra to run a perf sim and produce a cost delta estimate.

—Marcus

- Service credits only, no automatic termination for a single monthly miss (we can include termination rights for persistent failure over N months).
- Define measurement windows and monitoring sources (Redwood telemetry; Orion may request independent logs).

Perf sim results (summary):

- Baseline: hosted multi-tenant average p95 for gen calls in US: ~85ms.
- With Dedicated + warm pools sized for Orion's projected QPS (6k rps): p95 ~48–62ms depending on prompt length distribution.
- To reliably get to 45ms p95 across all traffic shapes we need ~1.6–1.8x capacity (and optimized kernel selection for short-context fast-path).
- Estimated uplift: +55% on inference cost + $30k/month reserved capacity baseline (ballpark).

Recommendation (commercially pragmatic):
1) Offer: Dedicated reserved pool + premium support. SLA: 99.95% uptime + p95 <= 60ms for generation calls.
2) Charge: +50% on token spend plus $30k/month reserve.
3) Pilot: 60-day pilot with review; if metrics stable we can reduce to 99.99% / 50ms at a renegotiated price.

I can produce a short one-page technical appendix and SLO measurement definitions for Orion.

—Marcus
